- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is rising, model may overreact; reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply 1–3% downward bias in next 3–5 periods if sentiment weakens.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast curve with 1–2% dampening.  
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome by >3% over 3–5 periods, reduce forecast by 1–2% per period until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment drops sharply after a forecast spike, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70, model often overestimates; apply 2–4% downward bias if sentiment is weak or negative.
